verses.1: And the word of Jehovah was to me:
verses.2: And you went and called to the ears of Jerusalem, saying, “Thus says the LORD: I remember your kindness. I will take care of all your descendants after you. They shall go with me into the wilderness in this land, not a single one of them will be lost.”
verses.3: Holy is Israel to the LORD from the beginning. All their food will be poisonous; evil will come upon them, says the LORD.
verses.4: Hear the word of the LORD, the house of Jacob and all the families of Israel.
verses.5: So said Jehovah: What did your ancestors find in Me? They turned away from Me and went after the darkness. And they became dark themselves.
verses.6: And they said, “Who is this LORD who raises us up from the land of Egypt? He brings us into a land of darkness and gloominess, a land of deserts and ruins. No man can live there.”
verses.7: And I will bring you to the land of Karmel, so that you may eat its fruits and enjoy its benefits. Then you will enter and fill my land and my territory with destruction.
verses.8: The priests did not say, “Where is Jehovah?” The scribes and scholars did not know me. The wicked committed evil deeds against me. The prophets were sent away, but they did not return.
verses.9: Therefore, I will again wage war against you, O people of Jehovah, and against your children.
verses.10: For the birds flew over them, and they saw that they had been sent by God. They grew very tall, and they saw that it was indeed so.
verses.11: The people who worship God do so sincerely; but those who do not worship God, my people, they only seek to gain their own benefits at the expense of God’s honor.
verses.12: Let them be named “heavens” for this. Let their ruins be completely destroyed, says the LORD.
verses.13: For two evil deeds did my people commit against me. They abandoned me in the midst of living waters, to be buried in pits that they themselves could not cross.
verses.14: The servant of Israel, if he is born in that house, then he knows what it means.
verses.15: They would cry out like sheep. Their voices echoed throughout the land. Its cities were destroyed, and its inhabitants were killed.
verses.16: And the sons of Nof and Tahfanhes will also harm you.
verses.17: Do not do this! Abandon Jehovah your God at the moment you are being led away on this path.
verses.18: And now, what path shall I take? Should I go to Egypt to drink from the red water? Or should I go to Assyria to drink from the river?
verses.19: May your evil deeds be destroyed, and may your sins be forgiven. Know and see that evil and sorrow have left you, O LORD your God. I do not fear you anymore, O LORD, may your armies help me.
verses.20: For from a world I have entered into, I have been set free from your bonds. And you said, “I will not go away.” For on every hill and under every tree, you walk with great pride.
verses.21: And I will plant in you all the true seeds. And how will you become my vineyard laborers?
verses.22: For if you are caught in your sins, and you break your covenant, then I will bring you before My face. O LORD God, please have mercy on me.
verses.23: How can you say that I’m not buried? I didn’t go along with your ways. You know what you’ve done by making such a cheap deal of it.
verses.24: Pereh’limud Midbar be Avut Nafshah Shapah Ruach Tanatah. Who will bring her all those desires back to her? They won’t fly away during the new year.
verses.25: Let your feet be removed from sin, and let your heart be free from hatred. Then you will say, “I have not loved those who are foreign to me; I will go away from them.”
verses.26: Like a thief who is caught in his act, so too will those kings, queens, priests, and prophets of Israel be brought to shame when they are found in such a state.
verses.27: They say to the tree, “Father, you are our mother.” And to the stone, “You are the source of our life.” But when they face difficulties, they say, “Arise and save us!”
verses.28: And what is your God, who created you? Will he save you in times of trouble? For from the beginning, your God has always been Yahweh.
verses.29: Why do you all quarrel with me? Your sins have brought about this situation, O LORD.
verses.30: In your desperation, I have taken away your children. They were not allowed to eat anything. Your prophets became like wolves that destroy everything around them.
verses.31: You have seen what the LORD has done. I was a covenant between Israel and the land of Mefilah. But my people said, “Let us go back to our own land.”
verses.32: They forgot about her in their sorrow; her children and my people also forgot me over countless days.
verses.33: What is it that you should do to seek love for others? Also, learn from the bad things that happen along your path.
verses.34: Also, in your wings, there was blood from the souls of the ancestors. It wasn’t hidden at all; it was clearly visible on all of them.
verses.35: And I said, “I have committed no sin.” But he said, “Then why do you accuse me of sinning? I have not sinned.”
verses.36: How I wish you would change your ways, even from Egypt! As they are being destroyed by Ashur.
verses.37: And from this, I will also be unable to do anything; my hands will be useless on your head, for Jehovah will be angry with you, and I will not be able to help them.
